metadata.title: How To Use Order Bumps In Your Funnels To Increase AOV (New WPFunnels Tutorial)
metadata.author: WPFunnels - Drag And Drop Sales Funnel Builder
metadata.shortDescription:
Today, you will learn how you can use order bump offers in your Sales funnels.

👉 Join the WPFunnels Facebook Community: https://www.facebook.com/groups/wpfunnels/
👉 Get WPFunnels Pro today:
https://getwpfunnels.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video-descr&utm_campaign=order-bump-new

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In a typical customer journey,
- A person enters your funnel landing page
- He likes your offer and proceeds to checkout.
- Here, he pays for your offer product - let's say $100.
- And he then ends up on the confirmation page (or thank you page).

Here, you will earn $100 from a customer.

When using order bumps, the journey will have a slight change:
- A person enters your funnel landing page
- He likes your offer and proceeds to checkout.
- On the checkout page, he sees an order bump offer worth $30
- He sees that it's a relevant product and the cost is not high.
- The customer clicks on the order bump and it gets added to the cart as well
- He then pays for the offer product and the bump product - $100 + $30.
- And he then ends up on the confirmation page (or thank you page).

Here, you will earn $130 from a customer.

You could also try to upsell by offering an upgraded version of your main offer product as order bump.

In this video, you will see how you can set up order bumps for your funnels.

After watching this video, you will learn to
➡️ create & place order bump offers on your funnel checkout page,
➡️ customize the order bump content easily,
➡️ use various order bump templates to attract buyers,
➡️ create multiple order bumps for the same funnel checkout page,
➡️ replace main order with the order bump offer (if needed),
➡️ use discounts in your order bumps, and
➡️ change order bump position.

And eventually, you will start making 💲 more money 💲 from every buyer in your sales funnels.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In case you are new to WPFunnels, you may watch this overview video:
👉 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GrzIRl5jfBE

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An order bump is one of the best sales funnel tactics to help you increase the order value 💰 of every buyer who is about to purchase a product in your online store.

If you offer a relevant product or a better alternative as an order bump offer right on your checkout page, chances are the buyer will end up accepting the offer before making the payment.

This will not only help you increase the order value but also help you generate 💲 more revenue 💲 without any extra effort. At the same time, the buyer won't have to spend time looking for that product in the store, and will more likely be delighted with the offer (if you have made the right order bump offer).

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Video created using:
WPFunnels 3.4.14
WPFunnels Pro 2.3.2
WooCommerce 9.2.3

metadata.shortDescription:
Want predictable revenue instead of guessing your next launch?

In this episode of Quantum Business Queen, I break down the exact Self-Liquidating Offer (SLO) funnel strategy I use to scale online businesses — including real numbers, real return on ad spend (ROAS), and how low-ticket offers can fund your marketing automatically.

This is not hope marketing.
This is data-driven scaling.

But strategy alone isn’t enough — we also explore why frequency, alignment, and internal coherence determine whether funnels actually convert.

Inside this episode:

• What a Self-Liquidating Offer (SLO) funnel actually is
• Why freebie funnels attract dead leads
• How to use low-ticket offers ($17 / $47) to fund your ad spend
• Customer acquisition cost (CAC) explained simply
• How front-end offers cover ad spend and back-end creates profit
• Real funnel results (including 11:1 ROAS case study)
• How Video Sales Letters (VSLs) convert into high-ticket calls
• Why funnels eliminate marketing guesswork
• The ecosystem: email, podcast, Instagram, automation
• Why no strategy overrides energetic misalignment

If you’re a coach, healer, consultant, or online entrepreneur tired of inconsistent launches and relying on organic hope — this episode will change how you think about scaling.

Funnels create inevitability.

Alignment makes them convert.

—

https://sarahtynanquantumcoaching.as.me/alignmentcall

https://www.instagram.com/sarah.tynan.quantum.business/

00:00 – Why This Episode Is About Strategy

10:02 – Funnel Ecosystem & 85% Call Conversion
14:16 – Why Funnels Beat Organic Growth

metadata.title: How I Built an 11:1 ROAS Funnel (Self-Liquidating Offer Strategy for Coaches & Entrepreneurs)
metadata.author: Sarah Tynan
metadata.shortDescription:
If you’re relying on launches, referrals, or organic hope to generate revenue… this episode will recalibrate how you think about scaling.



In this strategy-focused episode of Quantum Business Queen, Sarah Tynan breaks down the exact Self-Liquidating Offer (SLO) funnel model she uses to build predictable, scalable online businesses — including real numbers, real ad spend, and real return on ad spend (ROAS).



This is data-driven marketing architecture combined with energetic coherence.



Because funnels don’t fix misalignment — they amplify it.

What You’ll Learn in This Episode

     
     
  •   What a Self-Liquidating Offer (SLO) funnel actually is
     
     • Why traditional freebie funnels attract uncommitted leads
     
     • How low-ticket offers ($17 / $47) can cover your ad spend
     
     • Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) explained simply
     
     • How front-end offers fund marketing and back-end drives profit
     
     • Real case study: $46,000 revenue in 6 weeks with $6,000 ad spend (11:1 ROAS)
     
     • How Video Sales Letters (VSLs) convert buyers into high-ticket calls
     
     • Why data eliminates guesswork in marketing
     
     • The ecosystem: email automation, podcast, Instagram, retargeting
     
     • Why energetic alignment determines funnel performance
     
     
What Is a Self-Liquidating Offer (SLO) Funnel?


A Self-Liquidating Offer funnel is a paid entry funnel where:


     
     
  •   The customer purchases a low-ticket offer upfront
     
     • The revenue covers or nearly covers the ad spend
     
     • The funnel effectively “pays for itself”
     
     • Backend offers generate true profit
     
     


Instead of attracting freebie seekers, SLO funnels filter for buyers.



This creates:


     
     
  •   Higher quality leads
     
     • Faster sales cycles
     
     • Stronger commitment
     
     • Scalable paid traffic systems
     
     


In today’s market, information is no longer power.

Implementation and environment are.

Funnel Economics Explained


Example breakdown shared in this episode:


     
     
  •   $47 front-end mini course
     
     • Customer acquisition cost ≈ $47
     
     • Ad spend covered by sales
     
     • Buyers move into VSL funnel
     
     • VSL drives high-ticket mastermind applications (~$15K offer)
     
     


In one six-week window:


     
     
  •   $46,000 generated
     
     • $6,000 ad spend
     
     • 11:1 Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)
     
     


This model removes reliance on unpredictable launches.

Why Funnels Beat Organic Guesswork


Organic marketing can build brand awareness — but it rarely provides scalable data.



Funnels allow you to:


     
     
  •   Target specific demographics and geographies
     
     • Analyze click-through rates, cost per lead, and buyer behavior
     
     • Make precise pivots
     
     • Scale what works
     
     • Stop “hoping” and start engineering revenue
     
     


Data creates inevitability.

The Funnel Ecosystem


A funnel is not just an ad and a landing page.



It integrates:


     
     
  •   Email automation sequences
     
     • Video Sales Letters (VSL)
     
     • Retargeting campaigns
     
     • Podcast content
     
     • Instagram authority building
     
     


By the time prospects book a call, they are warm.



Conversion rates can reach ~85% when alignment and ecosystem are strong.

Strategy Without Frequency Doesn’t Work


This episode also addresses a critical truth:



No marketing strategy overrides the laws of energetic alignment.



Funnels amplify what is already anchored.



If identity, coherence, and internal alignment are unstable — scaling will feel inconsistent.



Quantum Business Academy integrates:


     
     
  •   3D Strategy (funnels, ads, automation)
     
     • 4D Frequency Alchemy (identity recalibration + nervous system capacity)
     
     • 5D Creation (embodied deliberate creation)
     
     


Strategy creates structure.

Alignment creates sustainability.

Who This Episode Is For

     
     
  •   Coaches
     
     • Healers
     
     • Consultants
     
     • Service-based entrepreneurs
     
     • Experts tired of inconsistent launches
     
     • Business owners wanting predictable revenue
     
     


If you want scalable marketing that doesn’t require constant visibility, this episode is foundational.

Ready to Build Your Own Self-Liquidating Funnel?


Apply for Quantum Business Academy:



https://sarahtynanquantumcoaching.as.me/alignmentcall



Connect on Instagram:



https://www.instagram.com/sarah.tynan.quantum.business/

metadata.author: WP Course Lab
metadata.shortDescription:
Looking for the best paid entrepreneur mastermind community platform? This video ranks the top 10, from Facebook Groups to BuddyNext, with what each does well and where it falls short.
See the #1 pick, BuddyNext: https://buddynext.com

This ranked list compares ten options for building a paid entrepreneur mastermind community. Each gets one strength and one honest limitation. Then we explain why number one is different: a complete community platform on a WordPress site you own.

THE RANKED LIST, 10 TO 1
#10 Facebook Groups
Best at: Facebook Groups is where many masterminds start, because everyone is already there.
Limitation: There's no built-in way to charge members, you don't own the audience, and a private room of founders gets lost between everyone else's posts.

#9 Discord
Best at: Discord is great for live conversation, and its voice rooms suit a hot seat call.
Limitation: It started in gaming, newcomers find it confusing, and there are no courses or rich member profiles built around a paid mastermind.

#8 Slack
Best at: Slack is how many founder groups chat day to day, and it's fast.
Limitation: It has no way to take payment or manage tiers, answers get buried in channels, and a growing mastermind quickly outgrows it.

#7 Whop
Best at: Whop is built for selling access, so payments and memberships come together quickly.
Limitation: The community and learning tools are lighter, and your members live in their marketplace, not a space that's yours.

#6 Podia
Best at: Podia puts courses, community, coaching and email in one place, which keeps a small mastermind simple.
Limitation: The community side is basic, and you work inside their layout and their features.

#5 Kajabi
Best at: Kajabi is a strong all in one for courses, coaching and paid memberships, with polished checkout.
Limitation: It's built around selling content, so member to member conversation is secondary, and you work inside their templates.

#4 Mighty Networks
Best at: Mighty Networks handles paid communities, courses and events well, and offers a branded mobile app.
Limitation: It's a bigger commitment than a small mastermind needs, and the layout follows theirs rather than yours.

#3 Circle
Best at: Circle has a polished design, with paid memberships, spaces, events and courses in one place.
Limitation: It's still rented, so your members, your data and your terms depend on their platform and plans.

#2 Skool
Best at: Skool is simple, with a feed, courses, points and levels, and a paid group is quick to launch.
Limitation: Everything lives on Skool's platform and design, so your mastermind's brand comes second, and customizing the experience is limited.

WHY #1 IS BUDDYNEXT
BuddyNext is a complete community platform on a WordPress site you own. In the video you see its activity feed, spaces, member directory, events, partner directory, courses, memberships and your brand. Modular, not a fixed bundle: the others are described as one-size-fits-all, while BuddyNext is modular, so you switch on only what you need.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Coaches, operators and founders launching a paid mastermind who need private pods, hot seat calls, a member directory and tiered access in one place.

FAQ
What is the best platform to launch a paid mastermind community?
In this ranking, BuddyNext comes first: a complete community platform on a WordPress site you own. It covers activity feed, spaces, member directory, events, partner directory, courses, memberships and your brand.

Can I run hot seat calls on Discord?
Discord is great for live conversation and its voice rooms suit a hot seat call. The limits covered in the video: it started in gaming, newcomers find it confusing, and there are no courses or rich member profiles built around a paid mastermind.

Does Whop work for a paid mastermind?
Whop is built for selling access, so payments and memberships come together quickly. The community and learning tools are lighter, and members live in its marketplace rather than a space that is yours.

How do I keep a mastermind exclusive?
Give every pod its own space and set it to open, private or invite only. Membership tiers then control who gets into which room.

Start selling on Whop with no monthly fee: https://whop.com/new/?a=a1republic
Whop vs Skool: Where Should You Sell Your Online Course or Community?

Skool vs Whop compared side by side: Skool pricing vs Whop fees, what you actually get on each platform, the discovery pages, and how payouts work. If you want to sell an online course, run a paid community, or sell digital products, this breakdown shows which platform costs less and which one fits your business.

Timestamps:
0:00 skool vs whop where to sell your course
0:27 what is whop and what can you sell on it
1:18 what is skool community explained
1:50 skool pricing vs whop fees
2:36 skool vs whop real cost on $1,000 a month
3:24 skool features vs whop marketplace
4:41 do skool and whop bring you buyers
5:40 whop payouts vs skool payouts
6:53 skool or whop which is best for you
7:09 best platform to test an online course idea

Whop has no monthly fee and takes about 2.7% + 30 cents per domestic card sale, with extra for international cards. Skool has two plans: Hobby at $9 a month with a 10% transaction fee, and Pro at $99 a month with 2.9% + 30 cents. With 40 members paying $25 a month ($1,000 in sales), Whop costs about $40, Skool Pro about $140 and Skool Hobby about $120, so at low volume Whop usually wins on fees. Skool gives you a community feed, classroom, calendar, leaderboards and gamification, while Whop works as a storefront and marketplace for digital products, software, communities and Discord or Telegram access.

Go with Skool for online courses, coaching and active communities, and go with Whop for digital products, software, signals and Discord access. If you're just testing an idea, Whop is the easier place to start because there's no monthly fee. Neither platform will build your audience for you, so plan your marketing on Instagram, Pinterest, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok, and check payout speed, holds, withdrawal fees and chargebacks before you commit.

Websites & Tools Used:
Whop: https://whop.com
Skool: https://www.skool.com

📩 For video promotions email us at: contact@a1republic.com
🌐 Check out our website: https://a1republic.com

Disclaimer: Some links above are affiliate links, and I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This video is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice. Results vary and are not guaranteed.

metadata.title: Whop vs Skool 2026: Hidden Fees & Features
metadata.author: Click and Convert with Maria Sparagis
metadata.shortDescription:
Whop vs Skool: which is better for courses, coaching and high-ticket offers? Skool is a community-first platform focused on courses, memberships and engagement, while Whop offers a broader commerce and payments ecosystem for selling digital products and online offers.

In this Whop vs Skool 2026 comparison, I break down the key differences in features, pricing, transaction fees and payment processing — whether you're selling a digital course, coaching program or a $5,000+ high-ticket offer.

If you're comparing Whop vs Skool for an online course, coaching program, paid community or high-ticket offer, this episode will help you understand where each platform is stronger and what the differences can mean as your business scales.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Whop vs Skool 2026
00:51 What Are Whop and Skool?
02:11 Whop vs Skool Pricing & Fees
05:50 Payments & High-Ticket Sales
07:40 The Payment Risk Most Sellers Miss
10:12 Whop or Skool: Which Would I Choose?

#WhopVsSkool #Whop #Skool #OnlineCourses #CoachingBusiness

segments.text: If you're selling an online course, coaching program, or high ticket digital offer,
you've probably come across WHOP and skool. Now, both of these let you host your content, build
a community, and charge customers for access. But they're actually quite different, especially when
it comes to payments. And if you're selling a 2,000, $5,000, or $10,000 program, those
differences can potentially cost you thousands of dollars as you scale. My name is Maria Sparagis
and I am the founder of DirectPayNet. I've been working in payments for almost 20 years and I talk
to thousands of merchants every year that work on all these different platforms. In this episode,
I'm going to go over the major features of each of these platforms, what they actually cost, and most
importantly, what happens to your payments as your business gets bigger and bigger. Now, what are
WHOP and skool? Let's start with skool. Skool is really built around community and education. So,
you can create a community, host courses inside a classroom, run events, live streams, and calls,
and charge for access through subscriptions, or a one-time payment. Now, it also has a
big gamification component. And what I mean by that is that members earn points and levels by
participating in the community, and you can unlock content as you progress. So if you're a coach or
an educator and the community aspect is a major part of your product, then Skool becomes very
attractive. Alternatively, WHOP is a lot broader. So you can host courses, communities, and chats
as well as live streams, but WHOP is more commerce focused. WAP is going to allow you to sell digital
products and memberships, create checkout links, manage affiliates and subscriptions, and access
a much broader payments ecosystem. WHOP currently supports more than 100 payment methods, including
cards, wallets, payments, crypto, and a number of buy now, pay later options. So the simplest way
I'd describe them is Skool is a community first platform whereas WHOP is a commerce and payments
first platform and you have to keep in mind that that distinction becomes important when we look
at the cost. So let's talk about pricing. Skool currently has two plans. So you have the hobby
plan which is $9 a month but you pay 10% plus 30 cents on every single customer transaction.
Then Skool offers a Skool pro plan at $99 a month. If you take the pro plan, your transactions that
are up to $899 will cost you $2.9% plus 30. But here's something high ticket sellers need
to know. Once an individual transaction goes above $900, the rate increases to 3.9% plus
30. So let's use a real world example. Say you're on the Skool Pro plan and you're selling a $5,000
coaching program. On Skool Pro, a $5,000 payment at 3.9% plus 30 cents costs approximately $19530.
And don't forget, you're also paying $99 a month for your Pro subscription. Now, on the flip side,
let's look at WHOP. WHOP currently has no monthly subscription or setup fee for its
standard payments offering. And the advertised base rate for a successful domestic transaction,
for example, you're a US merchant and you're selling to Americans, that would be $2.7% plus
30. So that same $5,000 domestic credit card transaction starts at approximately
$13530. So that is a $60 difference on one $5,000 sales. So, if you make 20 of those sales,
that would make the difference $1,200. But as important as this is, I would not look at the
two numbers and automatically think, "Wow, WHOP is cheaper." WHOP's pricing is much more alocart than
what their current advertised price is. And let me give you one example. If you're a US merchant and
you have a customer that comes in internationally, they add an extra 1.5% for an international card.
And then if the customer decides to pay in their local currency, they add another 1%
for the currency conversion. Also, if you're using WHOP's automated billing functionality,
that's another 0.5%. So payment orchestration which can route payments between providers so
you can improve acceptance is another 0.8% when you enable it. Now what the payment orchestration
will allow you to do is to have a whole bunch of different payment options which is awesome for
you as a business owner so you can capitalize on all the different ways people are paying but 0.8%
is quite steep for this type of service. Also, WAP does offer tax calculation and remittance,
but it carries its own fee. So, as do affiliates, financing, and certain other fraud and dispute
tools. So, with WAP, you really need to ask which features am I actually going to be using, and
what's my effective processing rate after I add on all the features that I need? And that's the
major difference between these platforms. Skool's pricing is a lot more bundled and just easier to
predict. and for you to forecast at the end of the month. WHOP starts with a lower headline card
rate, but then you add more sophisticated payment functionality and add different payment modes and
so forth. And a lot of that functionality costs a lot more money and costs you extra and might
be difficult for you to forecast. Now, regarding payments and high ticket items and high ticket
sales, this is where I think WHOP becomes particularly interesting. WAP has put a lot
of emphasis on the payment experience itself. It offers local payment modes, AC, crypto, and
multiple financing and buy now pay later options. For example, its current financing options include
providers offering customer financing limits ranging into the tens of thousands of dollars.
And this can matter enormously when you're selling something that's like5 or $10,000. And you know,
you need to offer people different ways to pay for that. And as I mentioned earlier, WHOP also offers
payment orchestration. So instead of necessarily relying on a single path for every transaction,
WHOP can route transactions through different payments, different providers with the goal of
improving authorization rates and obviously making you more sales. So Skool's payment experience is
much simpler. The customer pays through Skool and Skool handles the payment infrastructure
and sends your payouts through Stripe Express. So essentially what Skool is doing is really focusing
on their infrastructure and they're outsourcing payments through Stripe and acting as a white
label for the payment services that they offer. Now Skool also supports subscriptions, one-time
payments, and high ticket transactions. Currently, up to 100,000 per transaction can be accommodated
on Skool. So, I wouldn't say Skool is bad for high ticket items. It's just that WOB gives you a much
deeper payment toolbox and gives you a lot more options to present to your customers. And as I
say often in my channel, the more payment options that you give your customers, the more sales you
will convert. But there's another issue I think growing businesses should really consider. When
you're using the native payment system on one of these platforms, you don't have the same payment
provider independence that you would have when you have your own e-commerce stack that you can
control yourself. Now, what that means is that you can't necessarily wake up tomorrow morning
and say, you know what, I'm going to get my own merchant account and I'm going to plug it to my
store's checkout. That can't happen. you need to be using one of the payment options that Skool or
WHOP is allowing you to use because that is their business model and that is how they make money by
allowing you to process transactions through their platform. They're, you know, helping you with the
technology and making sure that you're able to get everything integrated quickly and easily. But the
compensation here is that you're paying them for your transactions and they control your payments.
And think about what that means if everything is in one place. So you have your courses there,
you have your community there, your customers are there, your subscriptions are all lodged in there,
and as I said, your payments are there. So that's very convenient and that really helps everything
working properly. But if you've been following me along and you listen to some of my content,
you're going to realize that payment risk changes as businesses grow. Chargebacks can increase,
your business model can change, and your volume can spike unexpectedly overnight. A platform like
Skool or WHOP may reassess the risk at different times and make a decision upon whether they want
to support your business. So before building a large business entirely on any platform,
what you need to understand is what happens if my ability to accept payments through this platform
changes? What if they shut down my payments account? And as you know, I have a lot of
videos about Stripe and Shopify payments closing down accounts because, you know, somebody falls
outside of their risk appetite. And platforms like WHOP and Skool are just the same. They can just
shut you down if you get a couple of chargebacks or more refunds than they're expecting. So that's
not just a WHOP problem or a Skool problem. What the problem is here is that you're concentrating
everything about your business in one platform. And if that platform decides that you no longer
fit their risk profile and they don't allow you to process payments or accept credit cards or
any type of payment that you need to run your business, then all of the work that you put in
to build communities and your tech and so forth will be gone. Because if you can't accept credit
cards or other payment modes that you need, then effectively you're out of business. Now,
you're probably watching this and wondering which one should I choose? If I were primarily building
a coaching or education community and engagement, courses, events, and keeping everything simple
were my priorities, I definitely lean towards Skool. On the flip side, if I were building a more
sophisticated digital product or high ticket sales business, especially with international customers
or financing needs or a strong focus on payments because I have large tickets, for example, then
I take a very serious look at WP. Now, I'm going to add one more thing for you to think about. Once
your business has started processing substantial volume, I'd think about a third issue, too. So,
do I want my content and my payment dependent on one platform? So, you don't necessarily need to
duplicate your entire business, but you do need to have backups in case there's any issues with
WHOP or with Skool. And being in the business that I've been in for almost 20 years, I see a lot of
things like Stripe shutdowns or WHOP disabling payments or Shopify payments, for example,
adding a reserve. So, I like to make sure that growing businesses have some infrastructure that
they control themselves. Now, whether that's their website, their customer data, additional content,
or eventually a new sales channel that allows them to integrate their own payment solution. Because
you got to remember that the best time to think about a backup is before you actually need one.
For example, if you have a server, you likely have a backup server. If you have a customer service
agent, then you likely have a backup. So this is the same thing that you need to remember for your
payment processing. Relying on one provider can put your business at huge risk. Now the important
thing to keep in mind is if you're starting your business and you really need to focus on marketing
and getting clients and so forth, definitely WHOP or Skool is the best place to go because you need
to focus on making money before you start looking at the advanced basics as you know saving money
on payments or having backups and so forth. Now, if you're using WHOP or Skool right now,
let me know in the comments below what you're selling and which one you chose. And follow
along because I'm going to be looking at more of these platforms specifically on
the payments and on the revenue side. Thanks so much for watching and I'll see you in the next

So that's not just a WHOP problem or a Skool problem. What the problem is here is that you're concentrating everything about your business in one platform. And if that platform decides that you no longer fit their risk profile and they don't allow you to process payments or accept credit cards or any type of payment that you need to run your business, then all of the work that you put in to build communities and your tech and so forth will be gone. Because if you can't accept credit cards or other payment modes that you need, then effectively you're out of business. Now, you're probably watching this and wondering which one should I choose? If I were primarily building a coaching or education community and engagement, courses, events, and keeping everything simple were my priorities, I definitely lean towards Skool. On the flip side, if I were building a more sophisticated digital product or high ticket sales business, especially with international customers or financing needs or a strong focus on payments because I have large tickets, for example, then I take a very serious look at WP. Now, I'm going to add one more thing for you to think about. Once your business has started processing substantial volume, I'd think about a third issue, too. So, do I want my content and my payment dependent on one platform? So, you don't necessarily need to duplicate your entire business, but you do need to have backups in case there's any issues with WHOP or with Skool. And being in the business that I've been in for almost 20 years, I see a lot of things like Stripe shutdowns or WHOP disabling payments or Shopify payments, for example, adding a reserve. So, I like to make sure that growing businesses have some infrastructure that they control themselves. Now, whether that's their website, their customer data, additional content, or eventually a new sales channel that allows them to integrate their own payment solution. Because you got to remember that the best time to think about a backup is before you actually need one. For example, if you have a server, you likely have a backup server. If you have a customer service agent, then you likely have a backup. So this is the same thing that you need to remember for your payment processing. Relying on one provider can put your business at huge risk. Now the important thing to keep in mind is if you're starting your business and you really need to focus on marketing and getting clients and so forth, definitely WHOP or Skool is the best place to go because you need to focus on making money before you start looking at the advanced basics as you know saving money on payments or having backups and so forth. segments.text: Hello, love and welcome back. So, today we're going to be diving into the world
of online education, which is a $300 billion industry. Literally, everyone that I know seems
to be rushing to launch their latest course or community. And what most people don't know is
that 9 out of 10 communities never make it past year 1. That is actually quite alarming. So,
today I want to dive into the top online education platforms on the market and compare which one is
my favorite and why. Most people tend to pick their platforms based on Alex Hormozi or Iman
Gadzhi or whatever the hype is, but it's important to pick the platform that is right for your unique
business needs. Everyone online seems to say the same thing. Kajabi is your all-in-one. Skool is
for communities. Circle is for creators who want flexibility. And Whop is for scaling,
membership, and network marketing. The truth is all four platforms can technically do what you
need. The trick is in finding the right platform that can grow with you as your needs evolve. So,
let's dive into it. First, we have Skool. Backed by Alex Hormozi, Skool prides itself as
a community first platform, and it works. Their gamification system is brilliant. The numbers
prove it. Skool has grown to over a 100,000 active communities all in a matter of years. I personally
have joined dozens of both free and paid school communities, and that's honestly where I learned
so much of what I know about AI. You will find that the majority of business, entrepreneurship,
and AI communities are hosted on Skool. Another great benefit of Skool is that my friends who
are on school have told me that about 30% of their revenue and traffic actually comes from the school
explore page. 30% is a staggering number. I don't know about you, but 30% more revenue and traffic
to me is a no-brainer. But here's the catch. Skool locks you into their ecosystem, meaning
there's literally no way to white label it. You can't run it on your own custom domain. And if
you ever outgrow it, migration can get messy. If you're an educator that wants to launch fast and
doesn't care too much about the creative aspect of things, then Skool is definitely the right
community for you. Next up, we have Kajabi. Kajabi sells you this like all-in-one online education
building empire dream. And honestly, it's a great tool if you want a single login and are okay with
paying a little bit extra for convenience. But if you're the type that likes to geek out on
design or advanced automations like I do, then Kajabi can be extremely limiting. And that's why
after spending hundreds of dollars just testing out the Kajabi platform, I decided not to launch
my community on Kajabi. In fact, Kajabi's average turn rate is about 30%. Meaning that one in three
creators end up eventually leaving their platform, which just shows you that it's not great for
long-term growth. Kajabi is an incredibly powerful platform. I always ask people, are you building
a simple online course or are you building a long-term education platform? Knowing the
difference between the two will help you make your ultimate decision. Next, let's talk about Circle.
Backed by people like Ali Abdaal, Circle is one of those communities that isn't trying to be
anything. Circle is flexible. It integrates with all your favorite tools. And my absolute favorite
part is the design and customization. Honestly, it is a beautiful platform and there is so much
you can do in terms of customization. I love the user experience and the interface. It feels like
a platform that I want to spend more time on. It feels way more premium and high-end than school.
And that's why I am going to be launching my get educated.ai community on Circle. And if you'd
like to join the community for free, be sure to join the weight list at get educated.ai. Back to
the fact, the beauty of Circle is that it allows you to use your own custom domain, which I love.
So rather than going skool.com/geteducated.ai, I can go academy.geteducated.ai. Nobody even has to
know that it was launched on Circle. Here's a stat that most people don't realize. Circle has quietly
become the number one choice for seven and eight figure entrepreneurs. Why? Because serious players
value ownership over convenience. For me, the trade-off of having a custom domain alone is worth
it. Again, it really depends on what's important to you. Design and automations are so important
to me and that's why Circle feels like the right fit. And lastly, we have the new kid on the block,
wop.com. Backed by Iman Godzi. Whop has absolutely blown up over the past months alone. With over
500,000 active communities, and their angle is simple, speed and scale, Whop is like the Shopify
of communities on steroids. You can spin up membership products, plug into their marketplace,
and instantly get exposure to millions of buyers already browsing WOP's marketplace. Its biggest
strength is that it is brilliant for network and affiliate marketing. That can be super powerful
when you're starting from zero. The trade-off is again that you're building inside their
marketplace with literally zero customization and flexibility. So here's the question you should be
asking yourself instead of which platform is best. Ask yourself what's the most important to you.
Do you want speed to launch? If so, then go for school. Do you want simplicity under one roof? If
so, go for Kajabi. Do you want flexibility and branding? If so, go for Circle. Or do you want
marketplace and discoverability? If so, go for W. That's it, guys. The platform is literally just
a container. At the end of the day, it doesn't really matter which platform you choose as long
as you commit. Pick the one that gets you moving today. Whether it's Circle or Whop.com or Kajabi,
it doesn't freaking matter. What matters is that you start and you start now. Honestly,
picking the right community has been a major bottleneck for me. And while I am leaning
towards Circle, I haven't really fully made my decision yet. And so, I'd love to hear from you
in the comments which is your favorite community and why. And if you want the behind-the-scenes
look of how I'm building and launching my own AI community, be sure to hit subscribe!

Today we’re talking about the pros and cons of cohort-based vs. evergreen courses.

Join the Creator Network today: https://creatornetwork.com 
Big thanks to ConvertKit for sponsoring this episode! 
Join Brand Deal Wizard to Access "After Dark" episodes & become a supporter of the podcast: https://www.creatorwizard.com/bdw-overview

First of all, what’s the difference?

Well, a cohort-based course (often called a CBC) is usually a fixed period of time, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 90 days - and you go through the program with a cohort of your peers. They’re taught a few times a year, I just finished up Cohort #10 of my Brand Deal Wizard program for example.

However with evergreen (sometimes called on-demand) courses, students can enroll at any time. Typically you can binge all the course content like a Netflix show in as much or as little time as you want. 

And over the last year, I have experimented with converting my live cohort into an evergreen program.

And boy oh boy, do I wish I could reach back in time to Justin from 12 months ago, place my hand on his shoulder and tell him the pros and cons of cohort-based vs evergreen courses.

So by the end of this episode, you’ll know:

segments.text: As a course creator you've probably noticed that there's two primary ways that you might offer your
content up for sale. First, you have the idea of evergreen enrollment and this is the concept of
launching your course and then just leaving it up for sale indefinitely. The second is the concept of
holding multiple launches where you have a launch date for your course and then once that launch
period ends you're closing down enrollment until the next launch period. Well which of these is
best for your business? In this video I'm going to cover the pros and cons of both of these methods
as well as introducing a third approach that I believe covers the best of both worlds.
If you'd like to see more videos like this one helping you grow your online knowledge business
please click like and subscribe below hey everyone I'm Bryan McAnulty the founder of Heights Platform,
the online course creation software that helps you monetize your knowledge and get your students
results so first i'm going to cover the concept of evergreen enrollment now this is probably
the most popular strategy for most creators especially creators who are just starting out
because it's the simplest to implement basically you launch your course and then once it's launched
it's always up for sale and this gives you the benefit of having something where you
have the potential to get sales at any time so once your course is launched
you can always be getting sales for it you never have a period where it's impossible for someone
to buy from you and while these are the pros of evergreen enrollment you can run into some
disadvantages with this approach and one of them is from the standpoint of supporting your students
so depending on the course content that you have and the level of involvement you're going to have
in helping your students along the way it can become difficult over time to help students
with an evergreen enrollment structure because if you have a bunch of students joining here
and there all different times you run into this situation where everybody's at a different point
in your program or your course and it becomes a little bit harder to support everyone all at once
especially as an independent creator if you're going to eventually have a support team then
you can solve some of those issues and if you have things like a community discussion board or
something where students are also kind of helping each other along the way then that can be great
but that's one of the downsides of evergreen enrollment versus having everybody joining
your program at specific set times now the next downside is that it's harder to kind of build up
the idea of some hype around your content or your course or the idea of fomo where if you don't buy
it now you're going to miss out so when your course is always up for sale it's kind of like
somebody can always get it and you're relying on the idea of having discount codes or things like
that to kind of add to the scarcity and build up desire around your product now the idea of
multiple launches solves some of those problems that we have and the cons of evergreen courses
but it also comes with its own cons so having multiple launches you have the benefit of
first of all we're solving that problem where we now have this hype built around our course that
you want to purchase it as a customer because you are going to lose your chance after the
enrollment closes that's it so you have to make your decision now and that puts off
people from potentially procrastinating and maybe they want to buy your course but they just never
get around to it and it's always up for sale so they figure i'll just wait so that's one of the
benefits of having these multiple launches it gives you a reason to promote your course more
heavily during these times because it's only going to be open for enrollment at these certain times
and then it also does solve that con that we had with evergreen enrollment where supporting your
students is harder because they're all enrolling at different times so when you have these multiple
launches you know for a fact that all your students are joining your program at the same time
and all of your students are going to be at the same place in your program at the same time
so this allows you as a creator to say well i'm going to hold a live call with some of my
students and i know that i can support them all equally like in one call in one meeting something
like this because you know that they're all going through the same steps at the same time together
as opposed to somebody just starting out and somebody being almost at the end of your program
at the same time so this provides some structure for you as a creator but there are downsides so
the downsides to holding multiple launches is number one this is a lot more complicated than
evergreen enrollment you have to pick well when am i going to launch my course when am i going to
close it down and how many times am i going to do that per year how many students do i have to get
each time and does that match up with my revenue goals or student goals that i'm looking for
and that is something that can be very very difficult especially for a new creator where
it sounds enticing to be able to say well i'm going to launch my course here i'm going to
launch it again then and people will be more excited about it because it's launching only
at these certain periods well that's great but there's so much marketing effort that goes into
planning those launches so maybe creators are having a lot of success with multiple launches
but they're not really telling you how difficult it is to pull those off especially when you first
start with that so the other con with multiple launches is the idea that you run into this issue
where now you have all your students going through your program at the same time and you've planned
out this launch so you're able to get the students but if you're not able to actually handle and plan
out this workload really effectively then it might end up becoming too much for you to keep up with
if you don't pull it off correctly so what is the best way to sell your course then
well i believe that there is a place for both evergreen enrollment and having multiple launches
depending on the kind of course content you're selling and where you're at in your experience
as a creator but i also believe that there is a third option which kind of covers the best of both
worlds and i call this concept rolling launches now a rolling launch is the idea where you
are holding multiple launches throughout the year let's say you have a spring launch summer launch
fall launch winter launch and after the enrollment closes anybody who wants to purchase your course
is going to have to wait until the next enrollment to be able to get in so you're maintaining that
benefit of multiple launches where you know your students are all joining at the same time
they're going through at the same pace so you can understand how to support them better you're
maintaining that benefit of being able to have students joining at these different launches and
building up this hype around your program because it's not always available they have to join at
that time otherwise they've got to wait until the next time it launches but there's one really key
important difference here and that is the idea that a rolling launch after your program launches
on that launch date of that first course then it will be immediately up for sale for the
next launch date and enrollment period so you're capturing that benefit of the evergreen enrollment
where a student can always purchase from you at any time and this takes a real lot
of the pressure off of you as a creator to have to worry about well i have to do all this marketing
when my next launch comes up because otherwise with traditional multiple launches you say okay
i'm going to launch my course alright i got my students i was successful now i have to get them
all going through my program but then before you know it well i have to plan my next launch
and now it's a huge amount of effort well what if you could be getting some students coming
in and joining your program throughout that whole period and this captures this
really great option for you where let's say you have some students that they were
thinking about joining your program during this first launch and then they put it off
because maybe they saw your first email but then maybe you sent a bunch of other emails about the
program launch or the enrollment closing for this launch soon and the program going to start
and they just happen to miss those but maybe they would want to enroll like a week later now
with traditional multiple launches you could maybe make an exception for them but with these idea of
rolling launches you now have the option that that student can purchase still and they'll get access
to that next period so a student can buy from you at any time with rolling launches just like
evergreen enrollment so you have this benefit that you're capturing both the option to sell
your content at any time without the hassle of having to plan out this giant marketing initiative
and the option where you're able to support your students easier because they're all going through
your program and enrolling at the same time so for this reason i think that rolling launches is a
great way to go for a lot of creators and heights platform actually is software that supports the
idea of rolling launches really easily all you have to do is set the launch date for your program
and then when students purchase it they will get access on that launch date
as soon as that launch date actually happens all you need to do is go back to your course
and change to the next launch date that you're going to have then when your next group of
students purchase they're automatically going to get access on that next launch
date so your course is always up for sale and everything is already pre-scheduled for you
so i hope this video was helpful for you leave a comment below and let me know which strategy
you're going to go with for your online course is it evergreen enrollment having multiple launches
with a traditional multiple launch format or this concept of rolling launchers for your course
if you'd like to see more videos like this one specifically about how to pre-sell your
course and start getting sales for it before it launches take a look at this next video

metadata.title: 60: Why Evergreen Courses are Harder to Sell in 2026
metadata.author: Lydia Martin | Your Online Business Mentor
metadata.shortDescription:
In this episode, we’re talking about something many course creators are quietly feeling:


Evergreen courses are harder to sell right now.


But here’s the truth… courses are not dead.


The traditional, information-heavy, DIY delivery model is what’s struggling.


We’re living in what many are calling a trust recession. Information is everywhere. AI can generate strategies instantly. YouTube tutorials are endless. Buyers are overwhelmed.


And when information is abundant, it is no longer the differentiator.


Transformation is.


In this episode, I break down:


• Why information alone is no longer enough
• The real reason completion rates in evergreen courses are low
• How overwhelm is impacting today’s buyers
• Why students are looking for guidance, context, and accountability
• The identity shift from course creator to experience leader


I also share a behind-the-scenes example from my own Kajabi course, Countdown to Launch, and what changed when I shifted it from a traditional evergreen format to a live cohort-style experience.


The results were dramatic.


Completion rates increased.
Momentum improved.
And students experienced real transformation.


That shift reinforced something powerful:


People don’t just want modules.
They want momentum.


In This Episode, You’ll Learn:


• What the “trust recession” means for digital entrepreneurs
• Why evergreen courses feel heavier to sell in 2026
• The difference between modules and milestones
• How cohort energy increases engagement and implementation
• Why the delivery model, not your expertise, may be the real issue


Key Takeaway


If your evergreen course feels harder to sell…


The problem may not be your content.


It may be your delivery model.


Today’s buyers want:


• Context
• Accountability
• Guided implementation
• A clear pathway forward


Transformation comes from milestones, not modules.


Tomorrow, we’ll go deeper into what an experience-led offer actually looks like, including how launching structured cohorts can create more predictable revenue and stronger student outcomes.


And remember… clarity and impact come from action.


If your course idea has been sitting on the back burner for years, or you launched and heard nothing back, there’s usually one specific thing standing in your way. This free quiz takes just a few minutes and shows you which type of course creator you are, plus the next step that fits where you are right now.


Take the quiz at launchwithlydia.com/quiz (https://www.launchwithlydia.com/quiz) 


Explore all online business resources, courses, and programs at https://launchwithlydia.com

Looking for a platform to run your online business? Get a 30-Day Free Trial + training & support at https://launchwithlydia.com/kajabi

Connect with me:

  •  Instagram: https://instagram.com/lydiamartinbiz
  •  YouTube: https://youtube.com/@lydiamartinbiz
  •  Substack: https://launchwithlydia.substack.com

metadata.title: 62: How to Design a Profitable Cohort-Style Course in 2026
metadata.author: Lydia Martin | Your Online Business Mentor
metadata.shortDescription:
In this episode, I walk you through how to design a profitable and impactful cohort-style course in today’s market.


If evergreen courses feel harder to sell, the answer is not to scrap everything and start over.


It’s to evolve.


You don’t need a brand-new offer.
You need a better structure.


In this episode, I break down what a cohort-style experience actually looks like, how to structure it around milestones instead of modules, and why this shift dramatically increases student completion, testimonials, and predictable revenue.


Want to learn more?


Join Cohort Impact Accelerator. Doors are opening again soon at https://launchwithlydia.com/accelerator  


What Is a Cohort-Style Course?


A cohort experience means your students move through your program together, with:


• A clear start and end date
• Weekly structure and rhythm
• Live support and implementation
• Defined milestones
• Built-in accountability


Instead of a self-paced content library, your course becomes a guided experience.


And that changes everything.


What Works Best (From Experience)


Over the years, here’s what I’ve found works beautifully:


• A 4-week cohort → 3 major milestones
• An 8-week cohort → 6 major milestones


This pacing allows students to move forward without feeling overwhelmed.


This is intentional experience design. You’re not just delivering content. You’re designing momentum.


The 5 Core Elements of a Strong Cohort Experience


At a high level, every successful cohort-style course includes:

  1. A clear, specific transformation
  2. Defined milestones that organize progress
  3. A structured live rhythm
  4. Guided accountability
  5. An intentional relaunch strategy

When you launch a cohort two to four times per year, you build messaging clarity, stronger testimonials, deeper authority, and predictable revenue rhythm.


If You Already Have a Course…


You don’t need to rebuild. You need to restructure.


Instead of leaving students to move through your course alone, invite them to:


• Start together
• Progress through milestones weekly
• Show up to live Q&A or coworking sessions
• Implement inside community


Transformation, accountability, and guided implementation are what sell in 2026.


They increase reputation, loyalty, and long-term revenue stability.


It's time to evolve from a course creator to an experience leader and guide.


If your course idea has been sitting on the back burner for years, or you launched and heard nothing back, there’s usually one specific thing standing in your way. This free quiz takes just a few minutes and shows you which type of course creator you are, plus the next step that fits where you are right now.


Take the quiz at launchwithlydia.com/quiz (https://www.launchwithlydia.com/quiz) 


Explore all online business resources, courses, and programs at https://launchwithlydia.com

Looking for a platform to run your online business? Get a 30-Day Free Trial + training & support at https://launchwithlydia.com/kajabi

Connect with me:

  •  Instagram: https://instagram.com/lydiamartinbiz
  •  YouTube: https://youtube.com/@lydiamartinbiz
  •  Substack: https://launchwithlydia.substack.com

metadata.title: 61: Why Cohort-Style Courses Are Winning Right Now
metadata.author: Lydia Martin | Your Online Business Mentor
metadata.shortDescription:
In today’s episode, we’re building on yesterday’s conversation about why evergreen courses feel harder to sell in 2026… and we’re talking about what’s working instead.


Cohort-style courses.


Not because they’re trendy.
Not because evergreen is dead.


But because the market has shifted.


Information is no longer scarce. AI can generate strategies instantly. Content is everywhere. Buyers are overwhelmed.


So if information isn’t the value anymore…


What is?


Implementation.
Momentum.
Accountability.
Transformation.


In this episode, I explain why cohort experiences meet that need and why they are winning right now for digital entrepreneurs.


I also share how I’ve been using cohort-style delivery since the very beginning of my business… long before I even had language for it… and how launching my program The Digital Clutter Cure six times in two years generated over $200,000 in revenue and built the loyal student base that still supports my business today.


In This Episode, You’ll Learn:


• The difference between a cohort experience and a traditional evergreen course
• Why information alone no longer drives buying decisions
• How cohort energy reduces overwhelm and increases completion
• The power of accountability and shared momentum
• Why milestones create transformation more effectively than modules
• How launching structured cohorts can create repeatable revenue rhythm


A Key Shift to Consider


Cohort-style courses are not just about adding live calls.


They represent an identity shift.


You move from being a course creator…
to becoming an experience leader and guide.


Instead of asking, “What modules should I record?”
You ask, “What milestones must my students hit to experience transformation?”


Modules organize information.
Milestones organize progress.


And transformation is what today’s buyers are truly looking for.


A Question to Reflect On


If your current offer feels harder to sell, ask yourself:


Is it designed as a content library… or as a guided pathway?


Because transformation comes from milestones, not modules.


In tomorrow’s episode, we’ll get practical. I’ll walk through how I intentionally design cohort-style offers, including length, structure, pricing, and how to know if you’re ready to launch one.


And remember… clarity and impact come from action.


If your course idea has been sitting on the back burner for years, or you launched and heard nothing back, there’s usually one specific thing standing in your way. This free quiz takes just a few minutes and shows you which type of course creator you are, plus the next step that fits where you are right now.


Take the quiz at launchwithlydia.com/quiz (https://www.launchwithlydia.com/quiz) 


Explore all online business resources, courses, and programs at https://launchwithlydia.com

Looking for a platform to run your online business? Get a 30-Day Free Trial + training & support at https://launchwithlydia.com/kajabi

Connect with me:

  •  Instagram: https://instagram.com/lydiamartinbiz
  •  YouTube: https://youtube.com/@lydiamartinbiz
  •  Substack: https://launchwithlydia.substack.com

metadata.shortDescription:
Get your free personalized $100M scaling roadmap: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

DISCLOSURE 
Information shared here is for educational purposes only.  Individuals and business owners should evaluate their own business strategies, and identify any potential risks.  The information shared here is not a guarantee of success. Your results may vary.

metadata.title: Live Course Launch Vs Evergreen Course For Your Coaching Business
metadata.author: Yulia Tarbath
metadata.shortDescription:
Live course launch vs evergreen course for your coaching business 

What’s the best way for you to launch your online course in your coaching business – live course launch or create an evergreen course?

In case you don’t know the difference – having an evergreen course means that it is open for enrollment all the time, with students beginning the course any time they want.

With a live course launch, you launch it once for a period of time (usually the actual launch is 10-14 days long) and then you close the enrolment.

Which one is right for you, especially if you’re building your health coaching business online?

Well, first thing first – the health coaching niche is a very profitable niche to create a course and a health coaching program in.

We grew our own health coaching business to a six-figure level and we’ve done live course launches, as well as run our evergreen course.

In fact, we sold over $700,000 worth of courses and coaching programs online!

Live course launch has many different aspects that you MUST have in place if you’re a health coach or a coach in other areas.

It takes a lot of time, energy (and stress) to run a live course launch campaign.

You have to have a lot of pieces in place to launch your course.

It is also a high-risk strategy.

Think about it – you’re a beginner health coach and you’ve put months into creating a launching an online course.

You’ve invested in copywriters, launch programs, coaches, ads.

You rely on that course launch to bring you revenue.

You launch it and … crickets …. Not one person has signed up for it.

A big Facebook ads budget doesn’t guarantee you results, especially if you’re a beginner coach.

What’s more, now you’re not going to do another course launch for months to come as you cannot launch programs too often.

In contrast to that, a high ticket evergreen course is a totally different story.

If you build your high ticket skills, choose the right coaching niche and create the right client attraction plan, you can be having paid clients right away.

They will be able to join your evergreen course at any time.

So which strategy should you adopt to grow your health coaching business?

Let me tell you more in my video today! 

#courselaunch #evergreencourse #healthcoachingprogram


Remember to COMMENT, SUBSCRIBE and SHARE! 

❤ FREE TRAINING: How To Attract More Coaching Clients And Start Generating $5K-$10K+ Months Online As A Wellness Coach: https://yuliatarbath.com/training 

❤ Join my FREE Facebook community for Health Coaches: https://www.facebook.com/groups/thesixfigurehealthcoach/

❤ Work with me personally: https://yuliatarbath.com/apply

Thank you for watching! 

Your wellness business mentor, 
Yulia Tarbath

segments.text: Today, digital publishers are actively
abandoning opaque, unpredictable social
media algorithms in favor of direct
permission-based email distribution.
This profound shift is rapidly
accelerating commercial timelines. By
2025, the median time for a new
publication to generate its first dollar
of revenue dropped to exactly 66 days.
But facilitating this rapid acceleration
requires robust infrastructure. Beehive
is engineered as a centralized operating
system for independent media businesses.
Historically, solo operators faced a
severe operational bottleneck, managing
the friction of a highly fragmented
software stack. This diagram shows the
fragmented past of the creator tech
stack, an email provider, ad network,
website builder, and payment gateway.
Notice the shift on the right. A unified
media hub absorbs all four of these
isolated functions into a single
centralized infrastructure. We are going
to deconstruct how Beehive achieves this
by examining its SAS economics, its AI
workflow orchestration, and the hybrid
monetization engine driving its target
of a $50 million revenue run rate.
Surviving in the modern digital
publishing economy means replacing
rented social audiences with owned
unified technical infrastructure. The
architecture of any creator platform is
defined by its economic model.
specifically the choice between a
percentage-based revenue share and flat
fee software pricing. Substack operates
as a consumerf facing social network. It
is free to start but extracts a
permanent 10% tax on all gross
subscription revenue. For a new writer,
that fee structure removes barriers to
entry, but as an independent publication
scales commercially, a flat percentage
tax becomes a mathematical drain on
working capital. Beehive relies on a
tiered software as a service structure
based strictly on subscriber volume.
Most critically, it charges a 0%
platform take rate on premium
subscriptions. This chart maps retained
earnings over time, comparing a 10%
gross revenue tax against a capped
monthly SAS fee. At the $200,000 annual
recurring revenue mark, the models
diverge by exactly $20,000. Preserving
that $20,000 in working capital allows a
publisher to aggressively reinvest in
investigative reporting, operational
software, or paid audience acquisition.
By charging a 0% take rate, the platform
ceases to be a taxing authority. It
functions as a fixed cost utility,
actively incentivizing publishers to
scale their operations. The operational
layer of digital publishing is evolving
at the same pace. Relying on static,
one-sizefits-all email broadcasts is an
obsolete strategy. With the deployment
of Automations V4, complex B2B marketing
logic is now available directly to
individual creators. This Automations V4
flowchart shows multi-split branching.
Starting at the new subscriber node,
traffic flows into the acquisition
source split. Creators can route readers
based on acquisition channels, treating
LinkedIn differently than Twitter, and
run inflow AB testing to optimize sales
funnels directly within the journey. For
macrolevel strategy, random cohort
branches allow a publisher to run
sideby-side tests of entirely different
overarching systems, like comparing a
3-day aggressive sales sequence against
a 7-day educational nurture campaign.
Managing workflows of this scale
introduces heavy administrative
overhead. Bulk action tools allow an
operator to select and update dozens of
simultaneous workflow steps at once.
Automations V4 converts the newsletter
into a highly optimized automated funnel
for subscriber retention and sales. The
next major operational leap in digital
publishing replaces rigid deterministic
software limits with fluid contextaware
AI agents. Beehive facilitates this
through a model context protocol or MCP
server integration. This acts as a
highly secure bridge connecting a
publishers's live database to external
large language models. Standard APIs are
structured, versioned, and strictly
deterministic. If you provide the exact
same input, you will receive the exact
same output every single time. The MCP
is engineered specifically for
non-deterministic AI agents. It accepts
unstructured conversational queries and

✍️ Want to start writing online? Download this free Ultimate Guide to get started: https://yt.startwritingonline.com

🤖 Want to write online, start (or scale) a newsletter, and launch digital products? Come join me LIVE inside our AI Writing Skool: https://www.skool.com/ai-writing-skool

––– My Books –––

📗 The Art & Business of Online Writing: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0FWK4BQB9

📙 The Art & Business of Ghostwriting: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0FW4PWRSH

📘 Writer Career Paths: https://www.amazon.com/Writer-Career-Paths-Ways-Words-ebook/dp/B0GPR1G9NB

––– Socials –––

Twitter/X: https://x.com/Nicolascole77

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/nicolascole77

YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@nicolascole77

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicolascole/

Medium: https://nicolascole77.medium.com/

––– About –––

If you’re new to my channel… hey there! 

My name is Nicolas Cole and I’ve been writing online since 2007. 

Since then, I’ve generated over a billion views on my writing, written 10+ books, and built multiple 7+ figure writing-related businesses, including two of the largest writing programs on the Internet: Ship 30 for 30 & Premium Ghostwriting Academy. 

I have made millions of dollars writing online, so I fundamentally reject this narrative (pun intended) “nobody makes a living as a writer.”

Yes, you absolutely can make a living as a writer. In fact, you can make more than just a living. You can make tons of money as a writer… IF… you’re a digital writer, and embrace learning the new skills required to thrive in a digital world. 

Which is why I started this YouTube channel.

Consider me your Digital Writing Mentor!

On this channel I talk about:

- Digital Writing
- Fiction Writing
- Ghostwriting
- Writing With AI
- Self-Publishing
- Writing Services & Business Models

So if you have any questions, drop me a comment on any video and I’ll answer them in a future video!

Keep writing,

Cole

monetize your newsletter with the
Beehiiv ad network. With the Beehiiv ad
network, you can browse and accept
pre-negotiated ad deals from advertisers
like Nike, Netflix, Notion, HubSpot, and
more. And you can place these ads
directly inside your emails to earn
money from day one without having to
reach out to advertisers yourself. And
all you have to do is pick the offers
that make sense for your audience, and
then publish them. Let's get straight
into it.
To get started, log into your Beehiiv
account and go to monetize
and go to ads.
Here, you'll see a summary of your
earnings, how many ads you've run, and
any ads you've already claimed that are
waiting to be published. Now, from here,
head over to offers on the left-hand
side to see all the ad offers currently
available to you. Each offer will
display the advertiser name, how much
you earn per click or 1,000 opens, and
an estimated earnings amount based on
your publication's performance. Keep in
mind that each offer has limited
availability, so once it's filled by
other publishers, it will no longer be
available. So, make sure to claim and
publish the ads that you want before
they're gone. And it's important to note
that you can accept up to five offers at
a time, and once you claim an ad offer,
you'll have up to five days to publish
an email containing the ad before the
offer expires. Now, when you find an
offer that you want to run, click claim.
Now, you'll see a pop-up that will allow
you to select different versions of the
ad to run. One of them will be marked as
recommended, which is a good starting
point, but you can choose whatever
version you feel is best fit for your
audience. For example, here I can run
this ad with or without a logo, and
choose from different versions that have
different text and images. Note that any
ads with logos will display a logo
banner at the top of the email in
addition to the actual ad in the email.
Once you've selected your preferred
version, click the drop-down arrow next
to confirm and add to post, and here
you'll be able to add this ad to a new
or existing post.
Now, if you select add to existing post,
you can choose a draft you've already
started, and the ad will be inserted
there.
Alternatively, you can also claim and
insert an ad directly from a post by
typing {forward slash} add and claiming
an ad offer this way.
Now, once your ad is inside a post, you
can simply drag the ad to wherever you
want it to appear in the post. Note that
if the advertiser is paying per click,
it might make more sense to move the ad
up higher in the email. But, if you want

actual email, it might make sense to

entirely up to you. Now, if you decide

specific post anymore, or you want to

editor and click move to another post.

ads,
offers,
and claimed, and move the ad to a new or

claimed ads and allow you to select

offers. Now, that's it for this video.

out the other monetization tutorials on
our YouTube channel.

🔗 Watch my full free Digital Product Masterclass: https://youtu.be/RxypuPGBRPI

📲 Follow me on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/richardyuzee/

Most people assume the hard part of selling digital products is making one. Or growing a big audience. Or getting comfortable on camera. None of those turned out to be the bottleneck. The real reason most people paste a promo link everywhere and hear nothing back is a step almost everyone skips, the one that sits between someone seeing your content and clicking your link.

You'll learn:
1️⃣ What product arbitrage actually is, and why it works more like a marketplace than a side hustle
2️⃣ The one sort I run on a product marketplace before I look at anything else
3️⃣ Why the math behind your first sales needs far fewer buyers than most people expect
4️⃣ The "wrapper": the step most people skip, and where the sales actually come from
5️⃣ Four ways to build it on Instagram, ranked from weakest to strongest
6️⃣ Five faceless content formats, plus how to find topics already proven in your niche

This model takes a minute to explain and a lot longer to get right. A link on its own asks a stranger to trust you. A wrapper gives them a reason to. That difference decides whether a post turns into a conversation or disappears.

I also cover what most videos on this topic leave out: the real risks of building on someone else's platform, and why the trust you build with people is the one asset in this model nobody can take from you.

If you want to see how the full system connects, from the first post to the first conversation to the sale, I walk through it step by step in the free masterclass linked above.





















Disclaimer: The results mentioned are personal experiences or student case studies. They are not typical and are not guarantees of success. Building a digital product business requires effort, skill, and consistency; individual results will vary.
